content.title: When do NHL playoffs start? 2026 bracket, standings with field filled
content.text: April 13, 2026Updated April 14, 2026, 6:46 p.m. ETEditor's notes: Check out this file for the latest scores, standings and playoff bracket updates following games on April 14.Every NHL team now has a "clinched" or an "eliminated" symbol by its name in the standings after games on Monday, April 13.The rest of the season will come down to determining seeding.Thirteen of the 16 NHL playoff spots have been filled as of Sunday. Monday night, the Philadelphia Flyers, Anaheim Ducks and Los Angeles Kings grabbed the final three berths.The Flyers beat the Carolina Hurricanes, 3-2, in a shootout to set up a first-round matchup with the rival Pittsburgh Penguins. The idle Ducks got the Nashville Predators loss they needed in order to clinch. The Ducks and Flyers have been out of the playoffs a combined 12 seasons.The Kings clinched the final berth with a victory against the Seattle Kraken and the Predators' regulation loss.By getting a point in the overtime loss, the Hurricanes wrapped up the Eastern Conference title. The Buffalo Sabres clinched the Atlantic Division title on Monday.Here's what to know about the NHL standings, including the latest playoff bracket, Monday's clinching scenarios and the tiebreaker procedures for the 2025-26 season before the postseason begins on April 18: Avalanche beat Oilers and Golden Knights beat Jets: What it meansColorado won 2-1 in a shootout and the Golden Knights won 6-2. The Golden Knights now have a two-point lead on the Oilers in race for the Pacific Division title. Each has one game left. The Ducks are three back and have two games left. The Jets become the second consecutive team to miss the playoffs one season after winning the Presidents' Trophy. The Rangers did it last season. Kings beat Kraken: What it meansThe Kings hang on to beat the Kraken 5-3 and clinch a playoff spot. Anze Kopitar extends his final season in the NHL by setting up Adrian Kempe's game-winning goal. The Kings hold the second wild-card spot and would face Colorado in the first round. But they're one point out of the first wild-card seed and third place in the Pacific Division. That leaves open the possibility of a fifth consecutive first-round matchup against the Oilers. Kings lead KrakenSeattle moved within a goal of the Kings, but Adrian Kempe scored to make it 4-2 Los Angeles Kings with less than eight minutes left in the third period. Sabres beat Blackhawks: What it meansBuffalo routs Chicago 5-1 and clinches the Atlantic Division title. Quite a turnaround for a team that was in last place in the Eastern Conference in early December. But it took off after changing general managers and ended a record 14-season playoff drought, plus won their first division title since 2010. They will face the first wild card, currently the Bruins. Kings lead KrakenThe Kings lead the Kraken 3-0 after two periods. If they hang on, they clinch a playoff berth. Sharks beat Predators: What it meansNashville gets two late goals by Luke Evangelista but loses 3-2 in regulation. That hurts Nashville's bid to get the second wild-card spot in the West. The Kings get in if they beat the Kraken. The Predators' loss also clinches a playoff spot for the Ducks, who end a seven-season drought. Panthers beat Rangers: What it meansFlorida won 3-2 in what said Rangers goalie Jonathan Quick said would be his last NHL game. The 40-year-old retires with a 410-308-90 record, the most wins by a U.S.-born goaltender. Lightning beat Red Wings: What it meansTampa Bay's 4-3 overtime win moves the Lightning past the idle Canadiens into second place in the Atlantic Division. They would have home-ice advantage in the first round if the standings finish up that way. Tampa Bay and Montreal have won game left. Flyers beat Hurricanes: What it meansPhiladelphia's 3-2 shootout win gives both teams what they need. The victory allows the Flyers to clinch a playoff spot, ending a five-season drought. They will face the Penguins in the first round. The Hurricanes, meanwhile, pick up the point they need to clinch the best record in the Eastern Conference. They will have home-ice advantage in the first three rounds. Their first-round opponent is the second wild card, currently the Senators.Who's in the 2026 NHL playoffs?Eastern Conference: Carolina, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, Buffalo, Montreal, Tampa Bay, Boston, OttawaWestern Conference: Colorado, Dallas, Minnesota, Vegas, Edmonton, Anaheim, Utah, Los AngelesWho could clinch an NHL playoff berth today?The Flyers will clinch a playoff berth if they beat the Hurricanes. If they do, they will open the first round in Pittsburgh. Update: The Flyers win and clinch.The idle Ducks will clinch a playoff berth if the Predators lose to the Sharks. Update: The Predators lose, so the Ducks clinch and end their seven-year drought.The Los Angeles Kings will clinch a playoff berth if they beat the Kraken and the Nashville Predators lose in regulation. Update: Both happen and the Kings clinch.The Hurricanes will clinch the Eastern Conference title if they get at least one point against the Flyers or if the Sabres lose to the Blackhawks. Update: The Hurricanes get their point in a shootout loss and clinch the Eastern Conference title.The Sabres will clinch the Atlantic Division title if they beat the Chicago Blackhawks in regulation and the Tampa Bay Lightning do anything but beat the Detroit Red Wings in regulation. WC - wild cardNHL tiebreakers: What is the first tiebreaker in NHL standings?If two teams are tied in points at the end of the regular season, here are the tiebreakers:Regulation winsRegulation and overtime wins (ROW)Total winsMost points earned in head-to-head competition: If teams had an uneven number of meetings, the first game played in the city that has the extra game is excluded. When more than two clubs are tied, the percentage of available points earned in games among each other (and not including any odd games) shall be used to determine standings.Goal differentialTotal goalsWhen does the NHL regular season end?The NHL regular season is scheduled to end on Thursday, April 16, with six games.When do the NHL playoffs start?The NHL's Stanley Cup playoffs are scheduled to begin on April 18.
